extracted.intended_audience: researchers and teams applying for Wellcome Discovery Awards (established researchers and their institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for applying to the Wellcome Discovery Awards — a scheme funding established researchers or teams proposing bold, creative discovery research with potential to advance human life, health and wellbeing. Includes who can apply, how applications are assessed and detailed cost/eligibility rules for requested items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead applicant career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead applicant must be an established researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must have international standing as a research leader in your field; experience of leading innovative and creative research; a track record of managing and training others. If leading a team, must demonstrate ability to drive and lead a substantial collaborative research programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract type and salary arrangements for lead applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: At point of application you should have a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract, or the guarantee of one; your salary must be paid by your administering organisation for the duration of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have less than three years remaining on your contract, you must have secured your next position at an eligible organisation and provide a letter of support. If based in a low- or middle-income country you may request a contribution to salary only if you hold a permanent/open-ended/long-term rolling contract and must get salary from external grant funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team size and primary location
rubrics_metrics.description: An award can be held by an established researcher or a team led by an established researcher; team size usually ranges from two to eight applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary location for the research, including leadership, must be within the UK, Republic of Ireland and/or a low- and middle-income country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coapplicant contribution and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Coapplicants must make a significant and essential contribution to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include leading a strand of research or managing the programme. All applicants are expected to be involved in designing the research and preparing the application. Coapplicants can be at any career stage and based anywhere in the world apart from mainland China. They must be based at an eligible organisation that can sign up to Wellcome grant conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coapplicant salary and time-commitment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Coapplicants can request salary if they meet certain contract/time thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any coapplicant requesting salary must contribute at least 10% research time. If <80% time on the grant they can request salary proportionate to time (minimum 10%) and their organisation must guarantee space and salary support if salary can't be obtained elsewhere (post cannot be dependent on award). At 80% time they can request full salary and post may be dependent on award. If coapplicants are postgraduate research assistants at 100% time, posts need not be underwritten by the administering organisation and can be dependent on award. Coapplicants employed by charities, social enterprises or commercial organisations may request salary proportionate to time; amounts must be proportionate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators (definition and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators support delivery of the project but do not lead a specific component and are distinct from coapplicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of support: sharing facilities, providing access to data or organisations, providing subject-specific expertise. Collaborators do not have to meet eligibility requirements and are not required to give minimum research time. Collaborators cannot receive a salary or compensation for time; you can request costs to cover their expenses (travel, materials/consumables) directly related to the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research appropriate for the scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be from any discipline (STEM, experimental medicine, humanities, social science, clinical/allied health, public health), single-discipline or multidisciplinary. Must not fall outside what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research (applicants should check remit and what is not funded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organisation location eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The administering organisation must be based in the UK, Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country (apart from India and mainland China).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administering organisation is responsible for submitting the final application and managing finances. It must be able to sign up to Wellcome grant conditions; the administering organisation owns any Wellcome-funded IP generated by the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organisation legal status
rubrics_metrics.description: The administering organisation must be a not-for-profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible organisation types include higher education institution, research institute, healthcare organisation, charity or social enterprise. (Note: coapplicants can be based in commercial organisations, but the administering organisation must be not-for-profit.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Who cannot apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific ineligibilities for lead applicants and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are not eligible to apply as a lead applicant if you are the lead applicant on two other Discovery Award applications and are waiting for a decision. You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsuccessful you can submit one more full application for the same project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant changes are needed for the second application. You do not need to contact Wellcome before resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment weightings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed on proposal, skills & experience, and research environment with specified weightings (used at interview stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weightings: Research proposal 50%; Skills and experience (applicants and coapplicants) 25%; Research environment 25%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal evaluation (qualities expected)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be competitive, the research proposal must be bold, creative and high quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bold: aims to deliver a significant shift in understanding and/or provides a significant advance over existing methodologies/conceptual frameworks/tools/techniques; potential to stimulate new and innovative research. Creative: proposed approach is novel — develops/tests new concepts/methods/technologies or combines existing ideas in a new way. High quality: well-designed, clear, evidence-supported and proposed outcomes/outputs are feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skills and experience evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of applicants’ and coapplicants’ outputs, leadership and ability to deliver the programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will review research outputs and contributions to the research community; contributions to and plans for developing team members and other researchers; leadership and management skills and plans to develop these during the award; how the programme will be managed and led; if a team application, rationale for team approach, team composition (including approach to diversity, inclusion and career stage) and contribution of each member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research environment evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how the research environment will support the project and the team's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will review how you will contribute to the strategic aims of your organisation; how your research environment(s) will help develop your research capabilities, leadership and management skills; your experience of and plans for contributing to a positive and inclusive research culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and duration guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: You should ask for resources needed; average award size and scrutiny thresholds provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average Discovery Award ~£3.5 million. Applications above £5 million will be subject to additional scrutiny. Awards can be up to 8 years (average 7); may be less for some disciplines and may be longer if part-time. When applying, cost at 1.0 FTE and Wellcome will extend duration for part-time awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff costs — lead applicant salary rules by location
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the lead applicant can request salary depends on location and contract type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If based in the UK or Republic of Ireland, lead applicant cannot ask for their salary. If based in a low- or middle-income country, can ask for a contribution to salary if holding a permanent/open-ended/long-term rolling contract and must get salary from external grant funding. To claim salary you must contribute at least 10% of your research time and the amount paid will be proportionate to time contributed (e.g., 30% time -> 30% salary). The administering organisation must confirm need and guarantee salary support including any costs not covered by Wellcome, if they cannot be obtained elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff working on the programme (who can be funded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will cover salary costs of staff who will work on the grant (full or part-time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes research assistants/technicians employed on the grant, specialist service staff and technical experts (e.g., environmental sustainability, data analysis), project managers if needed, and support for disabled staff. PhD/Research Masters studentships not provided (see separate rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching buyout (humanities & social sciences)
rubrics_metrics.description: HSS researchers can ask for funds for teaching replacement to cover temporary replacement lecturer costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must retain at least a 10% commitment to teaching. Costs can cover up to 33% FTE of your contracted time, usually for a person at a more junior level than the postholder, and can be spread across the grant. If you already get buyout from another grant you can ask only for the period when you won't receive buyout from the other grant. A letter from your employing organisation confirming your contract includes a teaching commitment should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD/Research Masters fees policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome does not provide studentships on this award but fees for employed research staff may be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants employing research staff can ask for PhD/Research Masters fees for those staff: each applicant can ask for fees for up to two research staff (max eight per team). Research staff should be hired for specific research activities; fees not requested at application cannot be repurposed later. Early-career applicants may not supervise a PhD alone but can co-supervise with mid-career/established colleagues. Research staff are treated as staff and incur a lower fee than student rate; if no staff rate exists request the home student rate, or international student rate if no other rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cost salaries for research staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary costs should reflect appropriate employer costs and allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask host organisation to use their salary scales and include basic salary, employer contributions (statutory obligations, pensions), Apprentice Levy (UK), incremental progression, locally recognised allowances (e.g., London allowance). Allow for Year 1 pay awards using IMF 'inflation, average consumer price' if unknown. From Year 2 use organisation’s current pay rates; Wellcome will provide a separate inflation allowance for salary inflation from Year 2 onwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa, work permit and immigration-related costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Can request visa/work permit costs for named people funded by Wellcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes visa costs for partner and dependent children, associated appointment travel and essential English tests, and Immigration Health Surcharge costs for persons and dependents in the UK for six months or more. If person will be working in a low- or middle-income country, Wellcome will cover emergency evacuation cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability-related adjustment support
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and staff with disabilities or long-term health conditions can request adjustment support costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs include additional staff to help day-to-day activities, assistive technology (e.g., text-to-audio), care costs for assistance animals when travelling. Wellcome will not pay for capital/building costs (e.g., access ramps). Support is only for costs not covered by government/employer; if unknown applicants can ask for these costs after award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing professional development and research skills training costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can request contributions towards CPD and research skills training where employer provision is unavailable or inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to £500 per year for lead applicants, coapplicants and each member of staff employed on the grant if they are in a post of ≥12 months and working ≥50% FTE on Wellcome-funded awards, provided the employing organisation cannot provide adequate training. Training types include leadership, management, responsible conduct of research, diversity & inclusion, environmental impact of research, and research skills training (technical/disciplinary). Costs must be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and consumables
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay for materials and consumables required to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes laboratory chemicals, reagents, PPE above standard expected, printing for fieldwork, shipping/delivery/freight. Funds allowed to outsource specialised project elements to organisations not involved as applicants/collaborators on a fee-for-service basis (e.g., synthesising compounds, building devices, preclinical studies, large-scale data analysis). Use separate line items for each Contract Research Organisation involved; CROs must be able to sign Wellcome grant conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animals costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding rules for animal costs vary by administering organisation costing methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organisation uses full economic costing (FEC): can ask to buy animals if essential, and for charge-out rates for animal house facilities including running costs, licences, staff training, appropriate estates costs, cage/equipment depreciation (not building depreciation). Macaques used in UK must be sourced from MRC Centre for Macaques. Wellcome may not pay full charge-out if they've funded the facility significantly. If organisation does not use FEC: can ask for costs to buy/transport animals, running costs, staff costs, equipment maintenance, housing equipment, microbiological monitoring, waste disposal, licences, training, environmental enrichment; in these cases Wellcome will not provide estates costs, cage/building depreciation, or equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment purchase and maintenance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You can request equipment if justified and subject to use and availability criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchase allowed where item not available at administering organisation or through collaborations and you will be the main user with priority access (≥50% use for Wellcome-funded activities). Costs may include purchase, delivery, installation, maintenance and training. Second-hand equipment allowed if more environmentally sustainable. Wellcome will cover VAT/import duties if usual UK exemptions don't apply or for non-UK applicants if costs can't be recovered. Equipment maintenance covered where equipment is funded by Wellcome or another source, is essential to the project, is five years old (or will become five during grant), and is cost-effective/environmentally sustainable to maintain. Maintenance can be requested for small multi-user items if ≥50% Wellcome use and no mechanism to recoup costs; Wellcome will not provide maintenance where recoupment mechanisms exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer equipment and software
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer equipment and software costs that are reasonable and justified can be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers one personal computer or laptop per person working on grant (reasonable, market-rate, justified), software, software licences and other recurring computing costs linked to the project. Electronic Research Notebook/ELN software may be requested on a per-user, per-year basis for the duration of the project for ELN software approved by the organisation. Cannot claim ERN/ELN hardware or organisation-wide ELN software beyond per-user charges. Wellcome won't pay for significantly expensive items unless justified, installation/training costs, or access charges in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access charges to shared facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: You can request costs to access shared equipment, facilities or services if essential to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include materials/consumables, a proportion of maintenance and service contracts, and staff time costs for dedicated technical staff operating the facility. Wellcome does not cover estates/utilities, depreciation or insurance, or other departmental staff time (except where related to animal housing facilities). If facilities were paid for by a Wellcome grant, access charges only allowed if the grant has ended and running-cost support has ended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overheads (indirect costs) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on which organisations can request overheads and how they must be justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who can ask: higher education institutions, healthcare organisations or research institutes outside the UK; UK research organisation that does not receive core funding for overheads; charities, social enterprises or non-governmental research organisations. UK universities and commercial organisations cannot ask for overheads. Overheads can include estates, non-project administrative/support staff, and administration (finance, library, room hire). Total overheads should not exceed 20% of costs requested in application and must directly support the activity funded. Sub-awards: applicants can ask overheads on sub-awarded parts to listed organisations but UK universities cannot ask overheads for sub-awarded activity if their university will include sub-awarded funding in its annual report to the UK Charity Research Support Fund. Regranting: redistributed funds cannot be used to claim overheads; instead an allowance will be calculated against direct costs to facilitate administration. How to apply: include a Finance Director letter explaining calculation; if audited methodology exists include confirmation, source and review date; if not include a breakdown and confirmation that request represents true costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmentally conscious travel and travel policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel on grants should be done in an environmentally conscious way in line with Wellcome's environmental sustainability funding policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider video conferencing/hybrid meetings as alternatives. Where travel is necessary, consider low-carbon travel (e.g., train) even if more expensive. Economy flights allowed when train journeys are over 10 hours, or train not possible due to availability, safety, visa issues, or for exceptional personal reasons (disability, caring responsibilities). Wellcome will not pay for business class flights. You can ask for project-related resources as alternatives to travel and for accredited carbon credits to mitigate essential travel emissions (contact Wellcome for approval before submission if organisational carbon mitigation isn't in place).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference attendance and travel allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Caps and rules for conference attendance costs and associated caring support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual limits: Lead applicant £2,000; Coapplicants £2,000 each; Research and technical staff £1,000 each. Accredited carbon credits to mitigate conference travel may be requested in addition. Caring costs for staff employed on grant to attend a conference may be paid (if Wellcome funds the salary, the conference is directly related to research, costs are over normal care costs, and organiser/employer can't cover them) up to £1,000 per person per conference. Other essential travel (collaborative visits, sample collection, fieldwork) can be requested with justification and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outward/return travel and accommodation/subsistence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on allowable travel and accommodation/subsistence costs by duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect people to travel by train for journeys with end-to-end travel time ≤10 hours. Flights paid where train not available, safety concerns, visa/permit issues, disability/caring needs or end-to-end >10 hours. No business class. Up to one month: subsistence (accommodation, meals, incidentals) can be requested; use employer subsistence policy rates or HMRC rates. 1–12 months: reasonable rental costs only (including aparthotels); choose economical options. >12 months: housing costs paid (see overseas allowances for details). If from LMIC and working in high-income country for >1 and ≤12 months, can ask for up to £10/day for extra costs such as transport. Baggage/freight allowances also specified (e.g., up to 80kg for ≤12 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical insurance, visas and vaccination costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome will pay medical/travel insurance and visa/vaccination costs in defined circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If travelling outside home country, medical and travel insurance costs covered when you cannot access state healthcare. Wellcome does not pay medical insurance for trips to the UK/Republic of Ireland; for UK trips ≤6 months take travel insurance covering medical expenses; for UK stays >6 months Wellcome covers Immigration Health Surcharge instead. Wellcome will pay visas, vaccinations and anti-malaria treatment, and costs to access health system where mandatory for immigration application. If already in destination country, visa costs may be taxable; Wellcome will cover tax related to these costs. For working in LMICs, emergency evacuation cover paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional costs for staff spending time in another country can be requested under overseas allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible applicants: higher education institutions, research institutes, healthcare organisations, charities, social enterprises or non-governmental research organisations. Allowances are a contribution towards personal cost of carrying out research overseas (so applicants are not disadvantaged), provided assuming you pay income tax in home or host country and that you/partner won't receive equivalent allowances elsewhere. Allowances determined by time spent away and estimated as accurately as possible. Partners and dependents travelling with you for >12 months may be covered (definition of partner provided). Accommodation/subsistence allowances will be based on family/business need with maximums set per location (based on market data or in consultation with administering organisation). Contact Wellcome if you need help calculating costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract research organisations and outsourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Outsourcing specialised elements to CROs or external fee-for-service providers is permitted with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may request funds to outsource work (synthesising compounds, building devices, preclinical studies, large scale data analysis). Where multiple CROs are involved use separate line items for costs relating to each. Contract Research Organisations must be able to sign up to Wellcome grant conditions.
